title: Introduction to oncoPoS
text: oncoPoS performs Probability Success (PoS) calculations phase 3 oncology study using Bayesian Hierarchical model. prior model based data observed earlier study, design features phase 3 study assessed industry benchmark success. Bayesian framework used oncoPoS relies work (Hampson et al. 2022). See PoS Bayesian Framework vignette details. main functions oncoPoS run_stan gen_pos, generate PoS estimate standard error (SE) planned analysis running rstan. SE calculated p̂(1−p̂)/Ndraws\sqrt{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})/N_{\text{draws}}}, p̂\hat{p} estimated PoS NdrawsN_{\text{draws}} total number post-warmup MCMC draws. PoS estimate can generated without considering observed treatment effect earlier study, can incorporate prior ORR /PFS data described sections .

title: Probability of Success (PoS) Calculation for Oncology Pivotal Studies
text: oncoPoS performs Probability Success (PoS) calculations phase 3 oncology study using Bayesian Hierarchical model. prior model based data observed earlier study, design features phase 3 study assessed industry benchmark success. benchmark PoS specified via Beta distribution using mean variance, can derived historical success rates predictive models (e.g., random forest). framework supports single-arm two-arm early-phase designs allows indication-specific ORR–PFS regression surrogate endpoints used.

title: Probability of Success (PoS) Calculation for Oncology Pivotal Studies
text: early endpoint objective response rate (ORR) used predict phase 3 outcome progression-free survival (PFS), relationship varies cancer type. account heterogeneity, oncoPoS groups cancer indications five categories, associated distinct set ORR–PFS regression parameters derived prior Bayesian hierarchical modeling. Indication Groups Group 1: Hematologic malignancies Includes classical Hodgkin lymphoma (CHL), diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), follicular lymphoma (FL), multiple myeloma (MM), non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). Group 2: Gynecologic cancers Includes cervical, endometrial, ovarian cancers. Group 3: Thoracic malignancies Includes non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), small cell lung cancer (SCLC), mesothelioma. Group 4: Urologic gastrointestinal solid tumors Includes bladder cancer, gastric cancer, renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Group 5: Breast cancer Includes breast cancer. indication specified user, oncoPoS defaults using average ORR–PFS relationship across indication groups.

Design features phase 3 trial: Progression-free survival (PFS) primary endpoint target hazard ratio (HR) 0.7; Two analyses using group sequential approach planned; number target events analysis 370 468; approximate HR bound analysis 0.7790 0.8204; randomization ratio 2:1. phase 3 trial planned following promising results earlier phase 2 study, reported PFS HR (95% CI) 0.53 (0.31, 0.91). addition PFS, objective response rate (ORR) data available single-arm phase 2 trial, 40 responders 100 patients historical control response rate assumed lie 0.05 0.20. benchmark probability success (omega) modeled using Beta prior mean 0.3 variance 0.03, reflecting prior belief historical success rate similar studies. information synthesized oncoPoS::gen_pos() using Bayesian Hierarchical model generate PoS estimate:

title: Generate Beta Distribution Parameters for Omega — get_beta_params
text: named list elements: alpha First shape parameter Beta distribution. beta Second shape parameter Beta distribution.

title: Generate Beta Distribution Parameters for Omega — get_beta_params
text: Beta distribution parameterized two positive shape parameters, \(\alpha\) \(\beta\), can derived given mean \(\mu\) variance \(\sigma^2\) using: $$   \alpha = \mu \left( \frac{\mu(1 - \mu)}{\sigma^2} - 1 \right), \quad   \beta = (1 - \mu) \left( \frac{\mu(1 - \mu)}{\sigma^2} - 1 \right) $$ parameters allow flexible specification prior distributions, particularly useful prior belief derived predictive model earlier step (e.g., machine learning model estimating historical success probabilities).
